action_items.description: Fix spawn-consumer zombie/timeout handling. When a spawned process dies within the first 10 minutes and last_error indicates a network/git failure (not a logic error — check for 'timeout', 'connection', 'ETIMEDOUT', 'ECONNREFUSED'), park the task back to 'ready' with metadata.backoff_until = NOW + 10 minutes instead of incrementing retry_count. In the dispatch loop, skip tasks where metadata.backoff_until > NOW(). After 3 park cycles (30 minutes total), THEN increment retry_count and count as a real attempt. Current behavior: git timeout → retry_count++ → 4 retries → task cancelled → orchestrator re-creates → repeat. Tasks bd7db0a3, 97d3267e, e28c83f4 have been in this loop for 3 days.
action_items.reason: Secondary blocker for the 3 P1 UCs. Even when budget allows spawning, transient SSH timeouts exhaust all retries before any logic runs. Backoff-and-park preserves retry budget for genuine logic failures.

action_items.description: Add GIT NETWORK RESILIENCE rule to SOUL.md under '## Git Workflow': All git remote operations (push, fetch, clone, branch creation, ls-remote) MUST use a retry loop. Template: for attempt in 1 2 3; do git <operation> && break; echo "Git attempt $attempt failed, retrying..."; if [ $attempt -eq 2 ]; then git remote set-url origin https://github.com/LeonidaTheGreat/leadflow.git; fi; sleep 15; done. Only report branch-creation-failed if all 3 attempts fail — include the exact error from the last attempt. NOTE: this rule is NOT currently in SOUL.md (confirmed 2026-07-24 inspection). All other major rules are present — this is the one remaining gap.

action_items.description: Add POST-FIX GATE VERIFICATION rule to SOUL.md under '## What You Don't Do': After applying any fix to a failing gate, you MUST re-run the exact gate command before calling reportSuccess(). Required step: run the triggering command (e.g. `npm audit --audit-level=high`, `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `git status --porcelain`) and confirm exit code 0. If the gate still fails after your fix, do NOT call reportSuccess() — diagnose the remaining failure, fix it, re-run, then report. Current GATE-FIX PRE-CHECK (already in SOUL.md) covers 'check if gate already passes before writing code' — this rule covers 'verify your fix actually resolved it before closing'.
